subject: Accounting
title: Catching Al Capone
description: A fast breakdown of Catching Al Capone for builders.

hook.text: Al Capone ran a criminal empire. The FBI couldn't touch him—until accountants found his weakness: taxes.

buildup.text: IRS agent Frank Wilson spent years tracing Capone's income through bank records and spending habits.

discovery.text: Wilson proved Capone had unreported income of over $1 million—leading to tax evasion charges.

twist.text: The most feared gangster in America was brought down not by bullets, but by bookkeeping evidence.

climax.text: Capone was sentenced to 11 years—one of the earliest and most famous forensic accounting victories.

punchline.text: Bullets couldn't stop Capone. An accountant did.

quiz.question: What charge was used to convict Al Capone?
options: Tax evasion based on unreported income

details.summary: Al Capone, the notorious Chicago gangster, was ultimately brought down not by murder or racketeering charges but by tax evasion. This topic covers how IRS accountant Frank Wilson painstakingly traced Capone's unreported income and created the template for modern forensic accounting.
details.whyItMatters: The Capone case established the principle of 'following the money' as the most effective way to prosecute criminals who cover their tracks. It created the blueprint for financial investigations still used today.
takeaways: IRS agent Frank Wilson spent years reconstructing Capone's finances from ledgers, bank records, and witness testimony
The net worth method—proving spending exceeded legal income—was pioneered in the Capone prosecution
Capone was convicted of tax evasion in 1931 and sentenced to 11 years in federal prison

faq.question: How was Al Capone caught through accounting?
faq.answer: IRS accountant Frank Wilson traced Capone's spending to prove his expenditures far exceeded his reported legal income. Using the net worth method, Wilson documented Capone's lavish lifestyle—property, cars, gambling—that couldn't be explained by his claimed income of zero.

faq.question: Why is the Capone case important for forensic accounting?
faq.answer: It proved that financial analysis could convict criminals who were untouchable through traditional law enforcement. The net worth method pioneered in his prosecution became a standard forensic technique, and 'follow the money' became the guiding principle of financial investigations.
